title: Bingemans Centre Drive speed limit and strategic plan actions
subtitle: Gender-based violence epidemic declaration, natural gas rates, UW Innovation Arena space, Sunset Hills rezoning, Lived Expertise Working Group deferral
overview: Council raised the speed limit on Bingemans Centre Drive from 50 to 60 km/h and moved a boulevard multi-use trail there up to short-term priority. It deferred a decision on school-hours speed limits until the Region of Waterloo finishes reviewing its pilot project {{vote:m19}}.

Council approved the first actions of the 2023-2026 Strategic Plan {{vote:m11}}, set aside up to $450,000 for city space in the UW Innovation Arena {{vote:m12}}, and cut the natural gas supply rate from 20.85 to 16.70 cents per cubic metre from November 1 {{vote:m13}}. It also approved a rezoning for 1154 Queen's Boulevard {{vote:m1}} and declared gender-based violence and intimate partner violence an epidemic {{vote:m23}}.

Council deferred the Lived Expertise Working Group funding decision to September 25, with September funding continuing {{vote:m21}}. It approved a collective agreement with IATSE Local 357 {{vote:m29}}. Council also heard an update on the Age-Friendly Kitchener Action Plan and a request for an off-leash exemption for service dogs. Staff did not support the exemption, and no motion followed.

decisions.item: Bingemans Centre Drive and school zone speeds
decisions.detail: Council raised the Bingemans Centre Drive limit to 60 km/h, made its multi-use trail a short-term priority, and deferred school-hours speed limit changes pending the Region's pilot review {{vote:m19}}.
Council approved the initial set of actions for the Strategic Plan {{vote:m11}}.

Council allocated up to $450,000 from the Economic Development Investment Fund 2.0 for leasehold improvements at 280 Joseph St West and referred about $17,500 in annual common area costs to the 2024 budget {{vote:m12}}.
Council cut the supply rate to 16.70 cents per cubic metre from 20.85 for system gas customers effective November 1, approved delivery rates, and set quarterly reviews {{vote:m13}}.
Council approved the zoning amendment for Sunset Hills Estates Corp. and allowed minor variance applications on the lands {{vote:m1}}.
Council deferred the year-two funding and approach decision to September 25, 2023, while continuing September funding to the Social Development Centre Waterloo Region {{vote:m21}}.

Council declared gender-based violence and intimate partner violence an epidemic and will send the resolution to the federal Minister for Women and Gender Equality and Youth in support of frontline funding {{vote:m23}}.
Council approved the Memorandum of Settlement for the 2023-2026 collective agreement with IATSE Local 357 {{vote:m29}}.

debate: A delegate opposed any speed limit changes, citing Vision Zero, Complete Streets and the climate emergency. The delegate noted that staff said vehicles already exceed the posted limit on Bingemans Centre Drive. If the limit rose, the delegate asked for separated cycling facilities first, a sidewalk review and a pilot.

Age-friendly advisory committee delegates asked for an age-friendly lens on council decisions and for the committee to be consulted early. They also asked for printed information, since many older adults do not use social media. Councillors raised seniors' housing affordability, long-term care input and food insecurity, and staff said the strategic plan includes a review of direct programming.

A delegate with service dogs asked for permission to unleash them in certain situations, citing training, exercise and the risks of dog parks. Staff said the by-law has no exemptions and that Guelph's limited off-leash approach has caused complaints and disputes.

On the gender-based violence motion, the CAO noted that 'epidemic' usually implies a public health response, much like the climate emergency declaration. One councillor said the city could still use its voice on the issue, while another suggested provincial governments and schools also be included. The mover kept the wording as written.

On the Lived Expertise Working Group, staff said talks with the Social Development Centre needed more time and the pilot's end date was unchanged. One councillor said the deferral was meant to clarify what the city wants from the group.
